title: Introduce crosswave span mesh and annotated cost ribbons for invocation-level attribution
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Engineering teams need faster root cause for token-level cost spikes that originate from cross-stage interactions (eg. prefetch warmups combined with streaming backpressure). Current observability surfaces show per-token cost and per-span latency but lack a joined view that surfaces correlated phase anomalies and a compact, time-aligned cost ribbon for an invocation.

What this PR does: Implements a lightweight crosswave span mesh that stitches spans from multiple pipeline stages into a single invocation graph, emits a new instrumented metric stream called invocation.cost_ribbon (time-series of compact per-segment cost deltas), and adds a dashboard and alert tuning knobs to detect cross-stage scarcity patterns. The change includes: 1) a server-side span enricher that attaches stage fingerprints and kernel-queue tags; 2) an on-path aggregator that produces an invocation-level cost ribbon (compact array encoded as proto text) and a set of per-segment cost histograms; 3) a Grafana dashboard with coordinated heatmaps (span mesh) + cost ribbon sparkline; 4) an alert rule that uses cohort-aware thresholds to reduce false positives during planned warmup windows.

Design notes: The span mesh preserves original span ids and emits a synthetic mesh_id for joinable spans; enrichment is best-effort and falls back to span-only mode when context is missing. Cost ribbon is intentionally compact: we store up to 12 equal-time buckets per invocation with normalized cost weights and a ring-index; this supports efficient indexing and low cardinality queries. Alerts run as a two-stage check: a short-window anomaly detector (30s) followed by a cohort stability verifier (10m) to avoid noisy triggers from transient bursts.

Rollout plan: feature flag "obs.crosswave_mesh" added with default off for prod. Start with 10% of invocations in canary, monitor ingestion and query costs for the new metric (linked Linear ENG-3421). If ingestion cost delta < 2% and query latency stable, increase to 50% and then enable alerts for SRE. Full rollout only after a 72h canary with no alert storms.

Checklist:
- [x] span enricher and mesh_id generation
- [x] invocation.cost_ribbon emitter with protobuf compatibility shim
- [x] per-segment histogram exporter (+ retention knob)
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON + example links
- [x] cohort-aware alert rule + playbook notes
- [x] unit tests for encoder/decoder and sampler
- [x] e2e smoke that validates ribbon matches aggregated token-cost sample

Backward compatibility: All new fields are optional; services that don't understand cost_ribbon will ignore it. The encoder includes a version header for future changes.

Risks & mitigations: Higher cardinality if stage fingerprints are overly specific — mitigated by bucketing fingerprints to canonical kernel groups and a sampling cap. Dashboard panels are read-only and behind the feature flag to avoid confusing users.

Related work: Builds on token-cost-attribution groundwork (see ENG-2987) and complements existing prefix/KV cache telemetry. Helps RCA for incidents where model warmup + kernel contention cause sustained cost drift.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the mesh join semantics (span identity preservation), the compact ribbon encoding (we opted for a base64-compact proto text rather than JSON arrays), and the cohort threshold tuning logic (two-stage verifier). The dashboard JSON contains annotated example traces for offline replay.

release_notes: Add crosswave span mesh and invocation.cost_ribbon: new low-cardinality invocation-level cost ribbon and span mesh for cross-stage attribution. Feature behind flag obs.crosswave_mesh. Includes dashboard and cohort-aware alerting. Intended to improve RCA for warmup+kernel contention incidents.
notes_for_oncall: If alerts trigger en masse after rollout, disable feature flag obs.crosswave_mesh and run scripts/feature_flag_canary.sh to rollback canary. Playbook at docs/runbooks/cost_ribbon_playbook.md explains triage steps and how to extract ribbons for manual analysis.
